## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the screen-share fix works as described. The portal's screen-share stream carries only `media.class=Video/Source`, while v4l2 and libcamera camera nodes also carry `device.api`, so requiring a v4l2/libcamera source on the link's output side is what separates the two. PipeWire also closes an idle v4l2 node once its last link is released, so the `fuser` check does not see a permanently open webcam on a default install. The new test passes, and it fails as expected when the probe is changed to treat every `Video/Source` as a webcam, to count errored links, or to ignore links.

One issue affects cloning the widget, and presence detection is broader than "a webcam". Smaller notes follow.

### Cloning the widget drops its probe script

`omarchy plugin clone omarchy.camera` copies a flat widget's entry points plus any files listed in `omarchy.clonePaths`. [`Camera.manifest.json`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/0e267cfad450d9b410b40503ffc43fcdde97959c/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/Camera.manifest.json) lists no `clonePaths`, so the clone does not get `camera-busy.sh`:

```text
built-in widgets/                 clone ~/.config/omarchy/plugins/<user>.camera/
  Camera.manifest.json    ->        manifest.json
  Camera.qml              ->        Camera.qml
  camera-busy.sh          x         (missing)
```

The clone's [`Qt.resolvedUrl("camera-busy.sh")`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/0e267cfad450d9b410b40503ffc43fcdde97959c/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/Camera.qml#L20-L25) then points at a file that does not exist. Quickshell's `Process` fails to start, logs a warning and never emits `exited`, so `cameraState` stays `absent` and the widget never appears. The clone command itself exits successfully and enables the clone in place of the built-in.

**Impact:** following the manual's "Cloning a built-in to modify it" section gives a camera widget that is always hidden, with no visible error.

**Suggested change:** declare the script the way [`Tray.manifest.json`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/0e267cfad450d9b410b40503ffc43fcdde97959c/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/Tray.manifest.json#L20-L27) declares `TrayModel.js`. With this block added to a copy of the manifest, the clone received a byte-identical, executable `camera-busy.sh`:

```json
"omarchy": {
  "clonePaths": [
    { "source": "camera-busy.sh", "target": "camera-busy.sh" }
  ]
}
```

A camera case in `test/shell.d/plugin-clone-test.sh`, next to the existing tray assertion, would keep it covered.

### Presence and in-use checks count any `/dev/video*` node

[`camera-busy.sh`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/0e267cfad450d9b410b40503ffc43fcdde97959c/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/camera-busy.sh#L20-L32) globs every `/dev/video*` node, [shows the widget](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/0e267cfad450d9b410b40503ffc43fcdde97959c/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/camera-busy.sh#L73-L79) when any exists, and reports `busy` when `fuser` finds any process holding any of them.

| Situation | PipeWire camera nodes | Widget |
|---|---|---|
| Webcam plugged in, unused | 1 | idle (correct) |
| Only a metadata, codec or v4l2loopback node | 0 | idle (shows a camera) |
| Webcam unused, a same-user process holds a non-camera video node | 1 | busy |

PipeWire only creates `Video/Source` nodes for capture-capable devices, so it does not list these other nodes as cameras. One Omarchy-specific example, traced in source and not run on hardware: after a Cam Link 4K using Omarchy's relay setup is unplugged, its v4l2loopback nodes remain, and the widget keeps showing a camera.

**Impact:** the widget can show a camera, or "Camera in use", when no webcam is present or in use. This matters more for an indicator users may read as a privacy signal.

**Suggested change:** when `pw-dump` returned data, use the PipeWire camera count for presence, and fall back to the `/dev/video*` glob only when it did not. For the `fuser` side, pass only the device nodes of the detected cameras (for example from their `api.v4l2.path`) instead of every video node. Alternatively, describe the current behavior in the manual.

### Smaller notes

- **No timeout on `pw-dump`:** [`pw-dump`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/0e267cfad450d9b410b40503ffc43fcdde97959c/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/camera-busy.sh#L43) waits for PipeWire with no bound. If the daemon hangs, the probe never exits, `Camera.qml` skips every later tick, and the widget freezes on its last state. `timeout 2 pw-dump` would bound it.
- **Optional test improvement:** every test case sets all three `CAMERA_BUSY_*` overrides, so the shipped `fuser` and `pw-dump` branches never run. Disabling the real `fuser` branch still passes the test, and any non-empty `CAMERA_BUSY_OPEN_DEVICES` value reads as busy. Stub `fuser` and `pw-dump` executables first on `PATH` would exercise the shipped code.
- **Polling cost:** each bar (one per monitor) runs bash, `fuser`, `pw-dump` and `jq` every second, and each `pw-dump` is a new PipeWire client. Real per-tick cost was not measured. A single shared poller, or Quickshell's `Pipewire.links` with node properties for the PipeWire half, would reduce the work.
- **Enable command in the PR description:** `omarchy plugin enable omarchy.camera --section right --before omarchy.microphone` fails on the default bar with "could not find target widget omarchy.microphone", because the microphone widget is off by default. `omarchy plugin enable omarchy.camera` alone works and places it in the right section.
- **Manual table:** in `manual/05-the-top-bar.md`, the Camera row's explanation sits in the "Middle / scroll" column. It may read better as a dash there, with the sentence in the paragraph below the table.
